architecture: Dedicated management bot hosted inside the existing WWC controller; existing NSS MongoDB wallet and WWC Supabase registry; no data migration
implemented: One-time language selection and persistent encrypted setup drafts
SQL document delivery and activation checks
Store dashboards and owner-only platform overview
Four-language folder-based native settings console with previews, Premium icons and button styles
NSS wallet quotes, explicit confirmation, atomic existing ledger, durable receipt/outbox reuse
20 active stores by default with one lazy worker and bounded queue
Existing NSS menu and child subscription links route to manager when configured
Fresh npm test builds compiled worker fixtures before tests

limitations: External Telegram/Supabase responses are synthetic, without production network latency.
Controller registry is mocked; its database requests are excluded from worker HTTP totals.
Request/response sizes count JSON bodies only; TLS, headers, file transfers and catalog source sync are excluded.
This is browsing with 50 products, not real checkout/payment or 24-hour production load.

required_activation: Create a separate manager bot in BotFather
Apply central migration 0047 after previous migrations
Set WWC_MANAGER_TOKEN and WWC_MANAGER_USERNAME on WWC; matching username on NSS
Keep current shared secret, encryption keys, database URLs, public HTTPS origins and owner IDs
Run one NSS instance and one WWC platform instance
limits: Offline benchmarks use synthetic Telegram/Supabase responses and mock central registry reads
No real payment, hosting or physical handset verification
Capacity is active store count, not twenty permanent processes or a production latency guarantee
Monthly request estimates and hosting free-tier limits are documented separately
